name: typhimurium_cohort_enteritidis_ref
mechanism: Three Salmonella Typhimurium isolates are run through a SNP pipeline using a Salmonella Enteritidis reference genome (P125109, GCF_000009505.1). Typhimurium and Enteritidis are both serogroup O:4 and O:9 respectively, members of subspecies I, but differ by thousands of fixed SNPs and major chromosomal rearrangements in the rfb (O-antigen) region. Reads still map — Enterobacteriaceae are closely related enough for partial alignment — but: (1) thousands of fixed between-serovar differences are called as SNPs, inflating apparent diversity by orders of magnitude; (2) regions of chromosomal rearrangement fail to align, shrinking the core genome; (3) the phylogeny reflects serovar-divergence positions rather than true within-cohort variation. The pipeline exits 0 with a populated SNP matrix and phylogeny that appears valid but is biologically wrong.

known_behaviors.behavior: Maps reads successfully (Typhimurium and Enteritidis are ~98% ANI); reports thousands of SNPs per sample relative to the Enteritidis reference. The core genome shrinks in rearranged regions but does not collapse to zero — unlike the sample-swap case, a valid but wrong alignment output is produced.
Produces a core alignment with many SNPs. Exit 0. The SNP count appears to reflect a highly diverse outbreak, which is the opposite of the true epidemiological picture.

samples.description: Salmonella Enteritidis str. P125109 — WRONG reference for a Typhimurium cohort; same species but different serovar

download.command: datasets download genome accession GCF_000009505.1 --include genome --filename genome.zip && unzip -q genome.zip && cat ncbi_dataset/data/GCF_000009505.1/*.fna > assembly.fasta && rm -rf ncbi_dataset genome.zip README.md
